source: Wild type strains with this reporter have normal chromatin and do not grow on medium lacking lysine, but all three FACT mutants tested here express the reporter and grow (called the Spt– phenotype; Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6.

claim: All three FACT mutants tested express the lys2-128∂ reporter and grow on medium lacking lysine (the Spt– phenotype).
source: Wild type strains with this reporter have normal chromatin and do not grow on medium lacking lysine, but all three FACT mutants tested here express the reporter and grow (called the Spt– phenotype; Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6.

claim: The Spt– phenotype was not affected by the loss of Ubp10 or loss of Ubp8.
source: This readout of transcription initiation resulting from poor quality chromatin was not affected by the loss of Ubp10 (Figure 6A,B; the growth defects caused by combining ubp10∆ with FACT mutations were similar on -lys and complete media so they are not due to changes in the Spt– phenotype) or loss of Ubp8 (Figure 6A and not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6A-B showing no effect of ubp10Δ or ubp8Δ on the Spt– phenotype.

claim: Neither a ubp10∆ nor an spt16-11 mutant activated the cryptic promoter reporter gene.
source: We then tested the effect of ubp10Δ on expression of a cryptic promoter reporter, which supports growth in the absence of histidine if galactose-induced transcription of the reporter activates a cryptic promoter within the FLO8 gene (Cheung et al., 2008) (Figure 6D). While neither a ubp10∆ nor an spt16-11 mutant activated the reporter gene, the double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant displayed significant levels of cryptic promoter activation (compare Gal Complete and Gal -his in Figure 6C) whereas the double ubp8∆/spt16-11 mutant did not.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6C.

claim: The double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant displayed significant levels of cryptic promoter activation.
source: While neither a ubp10∆ nor an spt16-11 mutant activated the reporter gene, the double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant displayed significant levels of cryptic promoter activation (compare Gal Complete and Gal -his in Figure 6C) whereas the double ubp8∆/spt16-11 mutant did not.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6C showing growth on Gal -his medium.

claim: The double ubp8∆/spt16-11 mutant did not activate the cryptic promoter reporter.
source: While neither a ubp10∆ nor an spt16-11 mutant activated the reporter gene, the double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant displayed significant levels of cryptic promoter activation (compare Gal Complete and Gal -his in Figure 6C) whereas the double ubp8∆/spt16-11 mutant did not.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6C.

claim: The pob3-L78R mutation on its own robustly activates the cryptic transcription reporter and enables near wild-type levels of growth.
source: We were not able to see an effect of combining a ubp10Δ with the pob3-L78R allele because the pob3-L78R mutation on its own robustly activates the cryptic transcription reporter and enables near wild-type levels of growth (Figure 6C), again highlighting the different effects of different FACT alleles.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 6C.

claim: Ubp10, but not Ubp8, acts in combination with FACT to maintain normal chromatin organization in the wake of RNA polymerase II transcription.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Ubp10, but not Ubp8, acts in combination with FACT to maintain normal chromatin organization in the wake of RNA polymerase II transcription.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section, based on the differential effects of ubp10Δ vs ubp8Δ on cryptic transcription in FACT mutant backgrounds.

claim: The structural changes that occur in canonical nucleosomes upon FACT binding are likely key to understanding how FACT stimulates the activity of Ubp10 on nucleosomes.
source: How does FACT stimulate the activity of Ubp10 on nucleosomes? While there is no direct evidence that FACT and Ubp10 work together in vivo, the synthetic genetic interaction and the biochemical cooperation that we observe is consistent with such a possibility. We propose that the structural changes that occur in canonical nucleosomes upon FACT binding are likely key to addressing this question, as the observed stimulation is specific to nucleosomal substrates.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism stated in the Discussion section, representing an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: FACT can reorganize the nucleosome by disrupting histone/DNA contacts, leaving the nucleosome in an 'open' or 'destabilized' state.
source: FACT can reorganize the nucleosome by disrupting histone/DNA contacts, leaving the nucleosome in an 'open' or 'destabilized' state (Chen et al., 2018; Kemble et al., 2015; McCullough et al., 2011) and by fully displacing H2A/H2B heterodimers (Belotserkovskaya et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2018; Hsieh et al., 2013; Orphanides et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2018; Xin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Chen et al., 2018; Kemble et al., 2015; McCullough et al., 2011.

claim: FACT can fully displace H2A/H2B heterodimers from nucleosomes.
source: FACT can reorganize the nucleosome by disrupting histone/DNA contacts, leaving the nucleosome in an 'open' or 'destabilized' state (Chen et al., 2018; Kemble et al., 2015; McCullough et al., 2011) and by fully displacing H2A/H2B heterodimers (Belotserkovskaya et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2018; Hsieh et al., 2013; Orphanides et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2018; Xin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Belotserkovskaya et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2018; Hsieh et al., 2013; Orphanides et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2018; Xin et al., 2009.

claim: H2A-H2B displacement by FACT has been estimated to be limited to 20–50% of the total heterodimers.
source: However, H2A-H2B displacement has been estimated to be limited to 20–50% of the total heterodimers (Orphanides et al., 1998; Xin et al., 2009) and requires the addition of Nhp6 to yeast Spt16-Pob3, whereas we observe complete deubiquitination, and no requirement for Nhp6.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Orphanides et al., 1998 and Xin et al., 2009.

claim: H2A-H2B displacement by FACT requires the addition of Nhp6 to yeast Spt16-Pob3.
source: However, H2A-H2B displacement has been estimated to be limited to 20–50% of the total heterodimers (Orphanides et al., 1998; Xin et al., 2009) and requires the addition of Nhp6 to yeast Spt16-Pob3, whereas we observe complete deubiquitination, and no requirement for Nhp6.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Orphanides et al., 1998 and Xin et al., 2009.

claim: Dimer displacement can only partially explain the effect of FACT on Ubp10 activity.
source: Dimer displacement can therefore only partially explain the effect of FACT.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, based on the observation that complete deubiquitination occurs without Nhp6 and that displacement is limited to 20-50% of dimers.

claim: An H2A/H2B-Ub dimer bound to FACT can be rapidly deubiquitinated by Ubp10.
source: While it is not known whether ejected H2A/H2B heterodimers retain the H2B-K123 ubiquitin modification in vivo, our in vitro results clearly show that an H2A/H2B-Ub dimer bound to FACT can be rapidly deubiquitinated by Ubp10.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, based on the in vitro deubiquitination assays.

claim: It is unlikely that FACT stimulates Ubp10 by recruiting it to the nucleosome, as there is no evidence that FACT enhances Ubp10 binding.
source: We think it is unlikely that FACT stimulates Ubp10 by recruiting it to the nucleosome, as we see no evidence that FACT enhances Ubp10 binding (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, based on the EMSA data showing no enhanced binding of Ubp10 to nucleosomes in the presence of FACT.

claim: The enhancement of Ubp10 activity by FACT provides the first example of a physiologically relevant substrate that appears to be activated by FACT-mediated destabilization of nucleosomes.
source: The enhancement of Ubp10 activity provides the first example of a physiologically relevant substrate that appears to be activated by FACT-mediated destabilization of nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, representing a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Ubp10 plays a global role in regulating nucleosome dynamics in concert with FACT, while Ubp8 plays a more restricted role at sites of transcription initiation.
source: Our results are consistent with a model in which Ubp10 plays a global role in regulating nucleosome dynamics in concert with FACT, while Ubp8 plays a more restricted role at sites of transcription initiation.
evidence: This is a model proposed in the Discussion section, representing an inference from the combined findings.

claim: Ubp8 is targeted to genes in the context of the SAGA complex, a global transcription factor that associates with promoter regions of virtually all RNA polymerase II genes.
source: Ubp8 is targeted to genes in the context of the SAGA complex, a global transcription factor that associates with promoter regions of virtually all RNA polymerase II genes (Baptista et al., 2017; Baptista et al., 2018; Bonnet et al., 2014; Venters et al., 2011), which accounts for the observed pattern of H2B-Ub enrichment in ubp8 deletion strains (Schulze et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Baptista et al., 2017; Baptista et al., 2018; Bonnet et al., 2014; Venters et al., 2011.

claim: The genome-wide pattern of H2B-Ub enrichment found in ubp10 deletion strains can be explained by a global function for Ubp10 in nucleosome assembly through its partnership with FACT.
source: The genome-wide pattern of H2B-Ub enrichment found in ubp10 deletion strains (Schulze et al., 2011) can be explained by a global function for Ubp10 in nucleosome assembly through its partnership with FACT.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Discussion section, representing an inference from the combined findings.

claim: FACT has been implicated in transcription through its increased association with frequently transcribed genic regions.
source: FACT has been implicated in transcription through its increased association with frequently transcribed genic regions (Feng et al., 2016; Mayer et al., 2010; Pathak et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2003), but these same studies show that it is also abundant in intergenic regions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Feng et al., 2016; Mayer et al., 2010; Pathak et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2003.

claim: FACT is also abundant in intergenic regions.
source: FACT has been implicated in transcription through its increased association with frequently transcribed genic regions (Feng et al., 2016; Mayer et al., 2010; Pathak et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2003), but these same studies show that it is also abundant in intergenic regions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by the same citations.

claim: FACT physically interacts with both the MCM replicative helicase and with DNA polymerase α.
source: FACT physically interacts with both the MCM replicative helicase and with DNA polymerase α, and it promotes rapid deposition of nucleosomes in an in vitro replication system (Wittmeyer and Formosa, 1997; Yang et al., 2016; Yeeles et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Wittmeyer and Formosa, 1997; Yang et al., 2016; Yeeles et al., 2017.

claim: FACT promotes rapid deposition of nucleosomes in an in vitro replication system.
source: FACT physically interacts with both the MCM replicative helicase and with DNA polymerase α, and it promotes rapid deposition of nucleosomes in an in vitro replication system (Wittmeyer and Formosa, 1997; Yang et al., 2016; Yeeles et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Wittmeyer and Formosa, 1997; Yang et al., 2016; Yeeles et al., 2017.

claim: FACT is found in yeast cells at about two-thirds the abundance of nucleosomes.
source: FACT is found in yeast cells at about two-thirds the abundance of nucleosomes and therefore is a global component of chromatin that participates in a broad range of chromatin-dependent processes (Gurova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Gurova et al., 2018.

claim: FACT is a global component of chromatin that participates in a broad range of chromatin-dependent processes.
source: FACT is found in yeast cells at about two-thirds the abundance of nucleosomes and therefore is a global component of chromatin that participates in a broad range of chromatin-dependent processes (Gurova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Gurova et al., 2018.

claim: Emerging evidence shows that FACT may have a less prominent role in proliferation of differentiated mammalian cells.
source: These roles include restoring chromatin integrity after disruptions like transcription (Martin et al., 2018) but emerging evidence shows that FACT may have a less prominent role in proliferation of differentiated mammalian cells (Gurova et al., 2018; Shen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as emerging knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Gurova et al., 2018 and Shen et al., 2018.

claim: The primary role of FACT is to stabilize or maintain existing global chromatin architectures and promote transitions to new patterns during differentiation.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest, instead, that the primary role of FACT is to stabilize or maintain existing global chromatin architectures and promote transitions to new patterns during differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Discussion section, representing an inference from the cited literature.

claim: Ubp10 has a global function in maintaining stable chromatin architecture against a range of potential perturbations.
source: The finding that Ubp10, but not Ubp8, plays an unanticipated role in DNA replication (Figures 4 and 5) and suppression of cryptic transcription (Figure 6) that overlaps with the role of FACT supports the idea that, like FACT, Ubp10 has a global function in maintaining stable chromatin architecture against a range of potential perturbations.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, representing an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: H2B ubiquitination has been proposed to stabilize chromatin as judged by a genome-wide reduction in nucleosome occupancy seen in mutants that lack Rad6 or in which wild type H2B is replaced by H2B-K123A.
source: H2B ubiquitination has been proposed to stabilize chromatin as judged by a genome-wide reduction in nucleosome occupancy seen in mutants that lack Rad6, the E2 that ubiquitinates H2B, or in which wild type H2B is replaced by H2B-K123A, which cannot be ubiquitinated (Batta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Batta et al., 2011.

claim: Deletion of UBP8 enhances nucleosome occupancy genome-wide.
source: Deletion of UBP8 enhances nucleosome occupancy genome-wide.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section.

claim: Highly transcribed genes have normal levels of nucleosome occupancy in a ubp8∆ mutant, even though these genes have markedly lower nucleosome occupancy in rad6∆ and H2B-K123A mutants.
source: However, the simple model that high global levels of H2B-Ub correlate with higher nucleosome occupancy is contradicted by the observation that highly transcribed genes have normal levels of nucleosome occupancy in a ubp8∆ mutant, even though these genes have markedly lower nucleosome occupancy in rad6∆ and H2B-K123A mutants (Batta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Batta et al., 2011.

claim: A double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant activates a cryptic promoter, pointing to a unique role for Ubp10 acting in concert with FACT to maintain nucleosome organization.
source: Our finding that a double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant activates a cryptic promoter points to a unique role for Ubp10 acting in concert with FACT to maintain nucleosome organization and is consistent with prior studies that suggest that cycles of both ubiquitination and deubiquitination are critical for nucleosome assembly during transcription (Batta et al., 2011; Fleming et al., 2008; Henry et al., 2003; Pavri et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, based on the cryptic transcription data in Figure 6.

claim: Cycles of both ubiquitination and deubiquitination are critical for nucleosome assembly during transcription.
source: Our finding that a double ubp10∆/spt16-11 mutant activates a cryptic promoter points to a unique role for Ubp10 acting in concert with FACT to maintain nucleosome organization and is consistent with prior studies that suggest that cycles of both ubiquitination and deubiquitination are critical for nucleosome assembly during transcription (Batta et al., 2011; Fleming et al., 2008; Henry et al., 2003; Pavri et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Batta et al., 2011; Fleming et al., 2008; Henry et al., 2003; Pavri et al., 2006.

claim: Ubp10 regulates spreading of heterochromatic silencing at telomeres and at mating type loci.
source: In addition to its role in regulating global levels of H2B-Ub, Ubp10 regulates spreading of heterochromatic silencing at telomeres and at mating type loci (Emre et al., 2005; Gardner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Emre et al., 2005 and Gardner et al., 2005.

claim: The silencing function of Ubp10 is mediated by the N-terminus of Ubp10, which is recruited by the SIR complex to subtelomeric regions.
source: This function is mediated by the N-terminus of Ubp10, which is recruited by the SIR complex to subtelomeric regions (Emre et al., 2005; Gardner et al., 2005; Zukowski et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Emre et al., 2005; Gardner et al., 2005; Zukowski et al., 2018.

claim: The silencing and global H2B ubiquitination functions of Ubp10 appear to be separable.
source: The silencing and global H2B ubiquitination functions of Ubp10 appear to be separable, as expression of N-terminal truncations of Ubp10 can restore wild type levels of H2B ubiquitination without restoring subtelomeric silencing (Reed et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Reed et al., 2015.

claim: A recent study reported that Sir2/Sir4, a subset of the SIR complex, stimulates the activity of GST-Ubp10 on both human nucleosomes and H2A/H2B-Ub heterodimers containing a hydrolyzable non-native linkage between ubiquitin and H2B.
source: A recent study (Zukowski et al., 2018) reported that Sir2/Sir4, a subset of the SIR complex, stimulates the activity of GST-Ubp10 on both human nucleosomes and H2A/H2B-Ub heterodimers containing a hydrolyzable non-native linkage between ubiquitin and H2B.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Zukowski et al., 2018.

claim: The observed stimulation by Sir2/Sir4 was attributed to the ability of Sir2/Sir4 to recruit Ubp10 to chromatin, as well as to a proposed allosteric stimulation of Ubp10 on both H2A/H2B-Ub heterodimers and on ubiquitinated nucleosomes.
source: The observed stimulation was attributed to the ability of Sir2/Sir4 to recruit Ubp10 to chromatin, as has also been observed in vivo (Emre et al., 2005), as well as to a proposed allosteric stimulation of Ubp10 on both H2A/H2B-Ub heterodimers and on ubiquitinated nucleosomes (Zukowski et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Emre et al., 2005 and Zukowski et al., 2018.

claim: The effect of Sir2/Sir4 on Ubp10 depended on residues 109–133 of Ubp10, which do not play a role in either Ubp10 catalytic activity on yeast H2A/H2B-Ub heterodimers, the ability to be stimulated by FACT, or FACT function in vivo.
source: The effect observed in that study depended on residues 109–133 of Ubp10, which do not play a role in either Ubp10 catalytic activity on yeast H2A/H2B-Ub heterodimers, the ability to be stimulated by FACT (Figure 3), or FACT function in vivo (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, based on the data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The effect of Sir2/Sir4 on Ubp10 appears to be restricted to its silencing-specific functions.
source: The effect of Sir2/Sir4 on Ubp10 thus appears to be restricted to its silencing-specific functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, representing an inference from the comparison with the Zukowski et al. 2018 study.

claim: Human Usp15 preferentially deubiquitinates H2A/H2B-Ub dimers and is stimulated by the splicing factor SART3.
source: Notably, human Usp15 also preferentially deubiquitinates H2A/H2B-Ub dimers and is stimulated by the splicing factor SART3 (Long et al., 2014), although in this case SART3 has the inverse effect: it enhances the activity of Usp15 on H2A/H2B-Ub but not on nucleosomes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Long et al., 2014.

claim: SART3 enhances the activity of Usp15 on H2A/H2B-Ub but not on nucleosomes.
source: Notably, human Usp15 also preferentially deubiquitinates H2A/H2B-Ub dimers and is stimulated by the splicing factor SART3 (Long et al., 2014), although in this case SART3 has the inverse effect: it enhances the activity of Usp15 on H2A/H2B-Ub but not on nucleosomes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citation to Long et al., 2014.

claim: Ubp8 is targeted to nucleosomes in the context of the SAGA DUB module, in which Ubp8 forms a complex with Sgf11, Sus1 and Sgf73.
source: Ubp8 is targeted to nucleosomes in the context of the SAGA DUB module, in which Ubp8 forms a complex with Sgf11, Sus1 and Sgf73 (Henry et al., 2003; Köhler et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Henry et al., 2003 and Köhler et al., 2010.

claim: The specificity of Ubp8 for H2B-K123 is conferred by Sgf11, which has a zinc finger domain with an arginine-rich patch that docks in the nucleosome acidic patch between histones H2A and H2B.
source: The specificity of Ubp8 for H2B-K123 is conferred by Sgf11, which has a zinc finger domain with an arginine-rich patch (Köhler et al., 2010; Samara et al., 2010) that docks in the nucleosome acidic patch between histones H2A and H2B (Morgan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Köhler et al., 2010; Samara et al., 2010; Morgan et al., 2016.

claim: Ubp10 has surprisingly high affinity for nucleosomes, binding with an apparent Kd of ~400 nM.
source: However, Ubp10 has surprisingly high affinity for nucleosomes, binding with an apparent Kd of ~400 nM (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Discussion section and demonstrated in Figure 3B.

claim: The wild-type Ubp8/DUB module does not bind detectably to nucleosomes by EMSA.
source: The wild-type Ubp8/DUB module, by contrast, does not bind detectably to nucleosomes by EMSA (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Discussion section and demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The ability of Ubp10 to bind nucleosomes and the stimulation of Ubp10 enzymatic activity by FACT do not seem to be connected.
source: The ability of Ubp10 to bind nucleosomes and the stimulation of Ubp10 enzymatic activity by FACT do not seem to be connected, as N-terminal deletions of Ubp10 that impair nucleosome binding are still stimulated by FACT (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section, based on the data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Deletions within the N-terminal unstructured region of Ubp10, which include residues important for recruitment to telomeres by the SIR complex, have little or no effect on global H2B ubiquitination.
source: Moreover, deletions within the N-terminal unstructured region of Ubp10 (Reed et al., 2015), which include residues important for recruitment to telomeres by the SIR complex (Kahana and Gottschling, 1999), have little or no effect on global H2B ubiquitination (Gardner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section, supported by citations to Reed et al., 2015; Kahana and Gottschling, 1999; Gardner et al., 2005.

claim: The significance of the ability of Ubp10 to bind nucleosomes and the use of nucleosomes as substrates for deubiquitination remains unresolved.
source: The significance of the ability of Ubp10 to bind nucleosomes, which was also observed by Zukowski et al. (2018), and the use of nucleosomes as substrates for deubiquitination therefore remains unresolved.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the Discussion section.

claim: There is no direct evidence that FACT and Ubp10 work together in vivo.
source: While there is no direct evidence that FACT and Ubp10 work together in vivo, the synthetic genetic interaction and the biochemical cooperation that we observe is consistent with such a possibility.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: The synthetic genetic interaction and the biochemical cooperation between FACT and Ubp10 is consistent with the possibility that they work together in vivo.
source: While there is no direct evidence that FACT and Ubp10 work together in vivo, the synthetic genetic interaction and the biochemical cooperation that we observe is consistent with such a possibility.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion section, based on the combined genetic and biochemical data.

claim: The proposed sequence of H2B ubiquitination, FACT-mediated nucleosome reorganization, then deubiquitination by Ubp10 and accelerated assembly could propel sequential assembly of nucleosomes, either in the wake of RNA polymerase or during DNA replication.
source: The sequence of H2B ubiquitination, FACT-mediated nucleosome reorganization, then deubiquitination by Ubp10 and accelerated assembly could propel sequential assembly of nucleosomes, either in the wake of RNA polymerase or during DNA replication.
evidence: This is a proposed model stated in the Discussion section, representing a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: This proposed sequence of events could also occur in humans, given the conservation of all components of this system.
source: This proposed sequence of events could also occur in humans, as well, given the conservation of all components of this sytem: RAD6B/RNF20/40 are the human E2/E3, USP36 is the homologue of Ubp10 and human FACT, Spt16/SSRP1, is the homologue of the yeast FACT complex, Spt16/Pob3/Nhp6.
evidence: This is a speculative extension stated in the Discussion section, based on the conservation of the components.
